hero.title: Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park (Medellín)
hero.subtitle: Medellín's green lung, navigating between traditional replicas and modern art. Enjoy a stunning 360-degree panoramic view of the city, stroll through the timeless corridors of a traditional Antioquian town, and experience the charm of modern sculpture art.

intro.title: Explore the Hill
intro.description: Discover the cultural landmark of Medellín, Colombia — a top-tier tourist destination that perfectly blends traditional architecture, contemporary sculpture, and magnificent city panoramas.  Located in the Belén district of Medellín, Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park is a unique cultural tourism attraction that perfectly combines 'traditional Colombian village charm' with 'modern sculpture art.'  Not only does it feature the iconic Pueblito Paisa traditional architectural complex, but it is also dotted with stunning sculpture works. From the mountaintop, you can overlook the magnificent scenery of the entire city of Medellín. Whether you're a traveler seeking cultural experiences or a photography enthusiast eager to capture city panoramas, you'll find your perfect experience here.

visitGuide.title: Visiting Tips
items: 🌞 Morning Tour: Start from the entrance ➔ Visit Pueblito Paisa ➔ Appreciate traditional architecture
🌙 Afternoon Sculpture Tour: Explore sculpture works in the park ➔ Taste local cuisine ➔ Experience cultural atmosphere
🎉 Evening Time: Enjoy sunset at the viewpoint ➔ Photograph city panorama ➔ Experience Medellín's night view

alsoKnownAs.title: Core Highlights
items: 🏛️ Landmark Pueblito Paisa: A complete architectural complex in traditional Colombian village style built on the mountaintop, including church, plaza, typical residences, etc. This is an excellent place to understand Colombian traditional architectural culture and the best spot to photograph Medellín's city panorama.

🎨 Sculpture Art Park: The park is adorned with numerous exquisite sculpture works, showcasing the elegance of Colombian contemporary art. These sculptures perfectly blend with the natural environment, providing visitors with a unique artistic experience.

🌆 Medellín City Panorama: The superior location on the mountaintop allows for a 360-degree overlook of Medellín's magnificent city scenery. During the day, you can appreciate the city layout; in the evening, you can photograph breathtaking sunsets and the bright city lights at night.

items.title: 🏛️ Stroll through Pueblito Paisa
items.description: Built in 1978, this is a perfect 1:1 replica of a traditional early 20th-century town in the Antioquia region of Colombia. Walk along the cobblestone square, visit the traditional church, town hall, and fountain, taste an authentic Bandeja Paisa, and experience the original Colombian charm.

items.title: 🎨 Immerse in the Modern Sculpture Park
items.description: As a sanctuary of open-air art, modern sculptures created by renowned domestic and international artists are scattered across the hill. The geometric lines of the art and the lush natural vegetation achieve a perfect balance here.

items.title: 🌆 360° Panoramic City Viewpoint
items.description: As one of the highest points in urban Medellín, it is a paradise for photography enthusiasts. During the day, the red-brick buildings spread across the valley like building blocks; at dusk, you will witness the breathtaking Andean sunset and the lighting of thousands of homes.

route.title: Visit Guide
steps: Morning (Cultural Exploration): Depart from the park entrance to Pueblito Paisa, visit the traditional church and plaza, and learn about Colombian architectural culture.
Afternoon (Art Appreciation): Stroll through the sculpture park, appreciate various contemporary sculpture works, and feel the cultural charm in the blend of art and nature.
Evening (Panorama Photography): Head to the mountaintop viewpoint, photograph Medellín's city panorama, and enjoy the magnificent sunset scenery and city night view.
supplements: Best Time: It is recommended to go in the evening, as you can enjoy both the daytime city scenery and the nighttime light show.
Sun Protection & Hydration: Medellín has a warm climate. Please carry sunscreen, sunglasses, and plenty of drinking water.

Photography Preparation: The mountaintop is an excellent location for photographing Medellín's panorama. It is recommended to bring a camera or ensure your phone is fully charged, and prepare for stable shooting positions.

scheduleItems.description: Walk up the hill from the entrance, weave through the lush sculpture park, and appreciate the art pieces.
Arrive at Pueblito Paisa at the top, visit the replica traditional buildings, and taste local street food (like Obleas wafers or fresh juices) in the square.
Head to the viewpoint, find the best spot, and take in the magnificent view of Medellín from sunset to the city lights turning on.

sections.title: Park & Culture
sections.content: Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park is an important tourist attraction in Medellín, carrying the development function of local culture and tourism. It has beautiful city views and traditional architecture, making it an ideal place to experience Colombian culture.

sections.title: Sculpture Art Function
sections.content: As a tourist attraction and sculpture art park, this is not only a leisure place for tourists, but also an important venue for local residents and tourists to experience artistic atmosphere. The park embodies the vitality and charm of Medellín's cultural arts.

transport.title: Getting There
transport.airportDesc: The closest airport to Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park is José María Córdova International Airport (MDE). Upon arrival, you can take a taxi or ride-hailing service to Medellín city center, then transfer to transportation heading to Belén district. The journey is about 45 minutes to 1 hour directly to Cerro de Nutibara, which is the most efficient way to arrive.

transport.busDesc: From Medellín city center, you can take buses or the metro to Belén district, then walk or take a taxi to the park entrance. It is recommended to consult local people for specific bus routes and schedules.

items.question: Where is Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park located?
items.answer: Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park is located on Cerro de Nutibara hill at Pueblito Paisa, in the Belén area of Medellín, Antioquia, Colombia. The Plus Code is 6CPC+H9.

items.question: Is Cerro Nutibara free to visit?
items.answer: Yes, Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park is a public space and is free to visit year-round. Some commercial and dining facilities inside may charge separately.

items.question: What is Pueblito Paisa on Cerro Nutibara?
items.answer: Pueblito Paisa is a faithful replica of a traditional early 20th-century Antioquian town, built on the summit of Cerro Nutibara in 1978. Visitors can stroll its cobblestone plaza, church, and heritage buildings.

items.question: What are the opening hours of Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park?
items.answer: The park is generally open daily from approximately 08:00 to 22:00. Hours may vary by season and weather, so please check Google Maps before your visit.

items.question: How do I get to Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park?
items.answer: From Medellín city center, the easiest way is to take a taxi or rideshare directly to the Pueblito Paisa parking lot at the top of the hill, or take the metro to Exposiciones or Industriales station and transfer to a taxi.

items.question: What sculptures can I see at the park?
items.answer: The sculpture park on Cerro Nutibara is an open-air museum with 10 permanent works, commissioned in 1983 by the Medellín mayor’s office with guidance from MAMM. Artists included Édgar Negret (Torre), Carlos Rojas, Manuel Felguérez, Sergio de Camargo, Carlos Cruz-Diez and Julio Le Parc, joined a year later by Otto Hajek. You can see them along the park trails between the entrance and the summit.

items.question: Is Cerro de Nutibara suitable for families?
items.answer: Yes, the park offers accessible ramps, public restrooms, and nearby parking, making it suitable for visitors of all ages.

items.question: What is the best time of year to visit Cerro de Nutibara?
items.answer: Any month works thanks to Medellín's spring-like climate. December to February and June to August tend to be drier, while April, May, September, October and November bring more afternoon showers. Mornings usually give the clearest views all year.

items.question: Where is Pueblito Paisa and how does it relate to the Sculpture Park?
items.answer: Pueblito Paisa sits on the summit of Cerro Nutibara, inside the same hill park that hosts the Parque de las Esculturas. The sculpture gardens on the slopes connect to Pueblito Paisa’s square by a short climb, so most visitors combine both in one trip.

seasonal.title: Seasonal Visiting Strategy
seasonal.subtitle: Medellín has no true winter: two drier spells and two rainier spells shape the year. The rows below reflect long-term average climate patterns, so pair them with the live forecast above before planning your day.
seasonal.note: Rows reflect long-term averages for orientation only; each year varies.

cols.advice: What it means for your visit

rows.climate: The driest stretch of the year: warm, mostly sunny days around 24–28 °C and cooler evenings near 17 °C.
rows.rain: Clear mornings with only occasional afternoon showers; skies stay open for long.
rows.nature: Evergreen forest remains lush; flowering trees, active birds and butterflies make it a fine season for nature spotting.
rows.advice: Best window for panoramic views and photography. On weekends, arrive at opening time to enjoy the quietest summit.

rows.climate: First wet season: warm and humid, with daytime highs around 27 °C.
rows.rain: Showers commonly arrive from mid-afternoon; mornings are often dry and bright.
rows.nature: Vegetation turns exuberant; mosses, orchids and bird calls intensify after the rain.
rows.advice: Plan photos for the morning, use midday showers for the covered galleries, and keep a foldable umbrella at hand.

rows.climate: A second drier spell with softer daytime heat (about 24–27 °C) and pleasant evenings.
rows.rain: Less rain than in March–May; brief showers can still surprise you.
rows.nature: The forest feels fresh after rains; hummingbirds and city birds are active early in the day.
rows.advice: A comfortable season for families and long stays. Late-afternoon golden light on the summit rewards photographers.

rows.climate: The second wet season: warm and humid, with frequent short downpours.
rows.rain: Rainy afternoons are the norm; mornings are the most reliable window.
rows.nature: Gullies and streams run fuller, and wildlife is easier to hear at dusk.
rows.advice: Walk early, watch for slippery sections after rain, and check opening status if a storm lingers.

stewardship.title: Science Corner & Visitor Responsibility
stewardship.subtitle: A hill is a museum without walls: it works as a living classroom and it only stays beautiful if everyone helps.

science.title: A city lung
science.text: The slope's trees capture dust and heat, cool the neighbourhood and slow rainwater runoff into the Aburrá Valley.

science.title: A small refuge of biodiversity
science.text: The secondary forest shelters dozens of bird species, tropical squirrels, butterflies and amphibians that find fewer homes elsewhere in the city.

science.title: An open-air cultural archive
science.text: Sculptures, heritage houses and the replica town make art and history visible to everyone, free of charge.

dos: Stay on marked paths and respect the fences.
Carry your rubbish out or use the bins provided.
Keep quiet at dawn and dusk to avoid disturbing wildlife.
Enjoy the sculptures from a safe distance without climbing on them.
Photograph flowers and animals without touching or feeding them.
donts: Feeding wild animals — human food harms them.
Picking plants or removing wood, seeds or rocks.
Smoking or lighting fires inside the forest.
Flying drones near people, viewpoints or wildlife.
Playing amplified music in natural areas.

legends.title: Stories & Legends of Cerro Nutibara
legends.subtitle: Beyond the viewpoints, the hill carries centuries of memory: indigenous names, colonial farms and a modern rebirth.
legends.intro: Some stories below are oral traditions retold by locals rather than written history. We mark them clearly and keep documented milestones separate.

items.title: The cacique behind the name
items.text: Oral tradition says the hill is named after Cacique Nutibara, a leader of the Nutabes people who lived in the mountains west of the Aburrá Valley before the Spanish arrived. Some stories describe the summit as a lookout from which chiefs watched over their valleys.

items.title: A border between worlds
items.text: Regional historians note that the hill long sat on the edge between different indigenous territories, and it still separates Medellín neighbourhoods today. That old role as a boundary may be why the hill kept its identity while the city grew around it.

items.title: From farmland to a city stage
items.text: During colonial and republican times the slopes were private farms and grazing land. In the 20th century the hill became public, and in 1978 a replica of an early-1900s Antioquian town — today's Pueblito Paisa — was raised on the summit to keep rural heritage alive.

items.title: When the hill turned into a gallery
items.text: In 1983 eleven local and international artists created large works directly on the hillside, encouraged by Medellín's modern-art scene. Walking between the sculptures today means walking through the same open-air museum those artists imagined.

items.title: A keeper of neighbourhood memories
items.text: For decades the hill has hosted first dates, school trips and New Year fireworks views. Ask any local and you will probably hear a personal story set on Cerro Nutibara — the strongest legend is the one the city keeps rewriting.

historyTimeline.title: Historical Origins: From Indigenous Totems to Public Park

items.title: The Legend of Cacique Nutibara
items.description: The hill is named after Cacique Nutibara, one of Colombia's most famous indigenous resistance leaders. Naming the hill Nutibara is a permanent tribute to the native history and anti-colonial spirit of this land.

items.title: Colonial & Republican Eras: Changes in Ownership
items.description: Early on, it was named Morro Marcela de la Parra after its female owner. In the 19th century, it was owned by the Cadavid family (Morro de los Cadavides) and served mainly as a pasture and stone quarry.

items.title: Return to Public Assets
items.description: Realizing its invaluable asset as an urban green lung and landscape core, the Medellín city government officially acquired it and planned it as a public park, beginning its modern transformation.

items.title: Pueblito Paisa Completed
items.description: As industrialization advanced, traditional rural towns in Antioquia rapidly disappeared. Guided by historians and architects, this perfect replica town was built on the summit as a rescue architectural experiment of historical and anthropological significance.

items.title: Open-Air Sculpture Park
items.description: Pushed by the Medellín Museum of Modern Art (MAMM), Cerro Nutibara welcomed permanent sculptures by 10 top international and local artists. It was an early Latin American attempt to combine avant-garde abstract art with natural public spaces.

geology.title: Geology & Ecology: An Urban "Green Island"
geology.subtitle1: Tectonic Origin: The Erosion-Resistant Andean Inselberg
geology.desc1: Geologically, Cerro Nutibara is a typical Inselberg. The hill is mainly composed of Cretaceous amphibolite and diorite, which are extremely hard. Over millions of years, softer surrounding rocks eroded away, leaving this core standing proudly.
geology.subtitle2: Ecological Value: The Aburrá Valley Sanctuary
geology.desc2: Covered with secondary evergreen broadleaf forests, including the native Guayacán tree. It is home to over 40 recorded bird species, tropical squirrels, and various amphibians, forming an invaluable ecological corridor within the city.

architecture.title: Architecture & Cultural Anthropology: Semiotics of Pueblito Paisa
architecture.desc1: Paisa culture blends traits from Spanish colonizers, Basque immigrants, and local indigenous people, forming a unique dialect, cohesive family values, and an iconic architectural style.
architecture.desc2: The central square features a typical Spanish grid layout; the traditional church replicates colonial white walls and red tiles; the barbershop, pharmacy, and school display real late-19th-century artifacts, educating the public about pre-industrial daily life.

art.title: Contemporary Art History: Breaking Museum Walls
art.desc1: "Signos en el espacio" (Signs in Space) by Carlos Rojas uses weathering steel to explore the conflict and symbiosis of geometry and nature. "La de la tercera edad" (Old Age) uses granite and metal to metaphorically represent the resilience of life.
art.desc2: The works cover Constructivism and Minimalism. They eschew figurative forms, using materials and spatial geometry to guide viewers in contemplating the relationship between humanity, art, and the hill itself.

didYouKnow.title: 💡 Hidden Easter Egg: Did You Know?
didYouKnow.description: Some of the wood, red tiles, doors, and windows used in the construction of Pueblito Paisa are actually authentic historical artifacts rescued and transported from the old town of El Peñol before it was flooded to build the Peñol-Guatapé reservoir!

about.title: About Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park
about.description: Welcome to **Cerro de Nutibara Sculpture Park**, widely recognized as the central **Cerro Nutibara**. Located in the heart of **Medellín**, **Antioquia**, **Colombia**, this destination serves as a primary hub for travelers visiting the region. As one of the city's largest "green islands," it not only preserves rich ecological resources but is also globally renowned for the Pueblito Paisa replica town and the open-air sculpture park at its summit. As a public asset, the attraction is currently managed and maintained by the **Medellín City Government (Alcaldía de Medellín)**, dedicated to providing a free and open space for natural recreation and cultural education for both locals and international visitors.

sculptures.title: The Sculpture Park's 10 Artworks on Cerro Nutibara
sculptures.subtitle: The sculpture park on Cerro Nutibara is considered one of Colombia's first open-air modern sculpture museums: 10 permanent works created in 1983 with guidance from the Museum of Modern Art of Medellín (MAMM).
sculptures.intro: Commissioned by Medellín’s city government and coordinated by artist Édgar Negret, the collection brings together Colombian and international creators. Each artist worked directly on the hill for around twenty days, fitting the work into the landscape.

works.name: Torre
works.material: Assembled and painted aluminium · 4 m high
works.note: An assembled aluminium tower true to the geometric-abstraction language of one of Colombia's great sculptors.

works.name: Untitled
works.note: A monumental concrete-and-steel volume: walk around it and watch the geometry shift with the daylight.

works.name: Signo aleteando al espacio
works.note: Added a year after the others, its open, colourful form seems to unfurl into space.

works.name: Construcción
works.note: The Mexican artist fuses iron and concrete in a large, ordered geometric composition.

works.name: Untitled
works.note: An abstract work that holds its own among the open green spaces and slopes of the hill.

works.name: Untitled
works.note: A small polished-marble piece: step close to watch the light play across the stone.

works.name: Estructura Cromovegetal
works.note: By the colour master Cruz-Diez, the work grows with living plants — art and nature together.

works.name: Construcción
works.note: A light tower of welded steel tubes whose lines read like a drawing suspended in the air.

works.name: Untitled
works.note: Iron and glass together make a piece that feels different at different times of day.

works.name: Untitled
works.note: A large-scale structure in fibreglass and aluminium that draws the eye from the trails.

sculptures.tip: The sculptures are spread between the hill entrance and the summit area. After exploring them, walk a few minutes up to Pueblito Paisa square to round out your visit.
